title: Có sạc không?
summary: Có sạc không? means “Do you have a charger?”

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Say Có sạc không? when you need "Do you have a charger". This is for when you need any charger before you explain more detail. This is the quickest recovery phrase when the battery problem can be fixed nearby. Listen for a yes/no answer, a gesture toward the item, or a short alternative; use the next rows if the exchange moves on.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: This pattern asks for a yes-or-no answer. Keep the main need together so the question feels natural.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use Có sạc không? as your first sentence for "Do you have a charger". This is for when you need any charger before you explain more detail. Pause after the phrase and listen for a yes/no answer, a gesture toward the item, or a short alternative. Show the phone screen or error message first so the problem is visible before you add more words.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Phone phrases work best when the other person can see the exact screen or error. For "Do you have a charger", Có sạc không? makes the next step easier to answer. If they point somewhere else, follow the gesture first and ask again only if the next step is unclear.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: In Phone, Internet & Power, the reply often comes as a yes/no answer, a gesture toward the item, or a short alternative. Say Có sạc không? once, pause, and watch for the reply. Show the phone screen or error message first so the problem is visible before you add more words.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: This is for when you need any charger before you explain more detail. It fits Wi-Fi, SIM, battery, charging, maps, and phone setup, especially when the next step is a yes/no answer, a gesture toward the item, or a short alternative. If they point somewhere else, follow the gesture first and ask again only if the next step is unclear.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Show the screen first and keep control of your phone unless the situation feels trustworthy.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Show the phone screen while you speak. A visible error message often explains the problem faster than more words.
